§9.2.7 Repeated Headers and Title Bands

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-repeated-headers-and-title-bands · tables boundaries headers

✅ Normative

Within one page, a column-header row printed again after data rows MUST close the table and open a new one at the repeat. Header repetition is the table-boundary signal.

| State | Rate |
| AL    | 1.10 |
| State | Rate |   ← header printed again after data rows:
| MT    | 0.95 |     the first table ends, a second starts here

Requirements

  • A re-declared header row MUST start a new table. The rows under it belong to that new table, not to the one above.
  • An entity or geography band that reappears as a title bar before each block likewise MUST open a new table each time it appears.
  • The repeated header MUST be kept: it is printed, so it is the new table's header row.
  • Two tables separated by a repeated header MUST NOT be fused, even where they read as one series broken up for layout.

✅ Sample — busbands

The Monday to Friday band with its AM/PM label reappears as a title bar before each stacked block, so each block is its own table.

Read it against the mirror case

If two fragments share a header that is not repeated, they are one table — see Split Tables Sharing a Header§9.2.9. Together, the two rules make header repetition the single boundary signal, decidable from what is printed without judging what the rows mean. An exception for a case that "obviously" continues weakens both rules and MUST NOT be made.

Across a page break

Across a page break, a repeated header is routine and says nothing about whether the table ended. That case is governed by Cross-Page Tables§4.3, not by this rule; within one page, a repeat is a boundary.

Related

  • Split Tables Sharing a Header§9.2.9 — the mirror case: an unrepeated shared header joins fragments
  • Cross-Page Tables§4.3 — a header repeated after a page break is not a boundary
  • Column Continuation§9.2.2 — side-by-side blocks, each with its own header copy
